questions.question: If (40√5x³ - 2√2y³) ÷ (2√5x - √2y) = Ax² + By² - Cxy, then find the value of A + 3B - √10C.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(40√5x3 – 2√2y3) ÷ (2√5x – √2y) = Ax2 + By2 – Cxy

**Formula used:**

a³ – b³ = (a – b)(a² + b² + ab)

**Calculation:**

(40√5x3 – 2√2y3) = [(2√5x – √2y)(2√5x)² + (√2y)² + 2√5 × √2]/(2√5x – √2y)

Comparing the value, we get

questions.question: A can complete a task in 6 days, while B can complete the same task in 12 days. How many days will they take to complete the same task if they work together?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Time taken by A to complete the work = 6 days

Time taken by B to complete the work = 12 days

**Formula used:**

Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculation:**

LCM of 6 and 12 is 12

Efficiency of A = (12/6) = 2 units/days

Efficiency of B = (12/12) = 1 unit/day

Time taken by A and B both to complete the same task together = [12(2 + 1)] days

⇒ 12/3 days

⇒ 4 days

**∴ The required time is 4 days**

questions.question: Suresh purchased a computer table for Rs. 9,000 and a centre table for Rs. 4,000. He sold the computer table with 8% profit. With what profit percentage should he sell the centre table so as to gain 10% on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of computer table = Rs. 9,000

Cost price of centre table = Rs. 4,000

Profit% for computer table = 8%

**Formula used:**

Profit = SP – CP

Profit% = Profit/CP × 100

**Calculation:**

Selling price of Computer table = Rs. (9,000 × 108/100)

⇒ Rs. 9,720

Total cost price of computer table and centre table = Rs. (9,000 + 4,000) = Rs. 13,000

Selling price of a computer table and centre table = Rs. (13,000 × 110/100)

⇒ Rs. 14,300

Selling price of centre table = Rs. (14,300 – 9,720) = Rs. 4,580

Profit of centre table = Rs. (4,580 – 4,000) = Rs. 580

Profit% of centre table = (580/4000 × 100)

⇒ 14.5%

**∴ The required profit% is 14.5**

questions.question: If 5 cos θ = 4 sin θ, 0° ≤ θ ≤ 90°, then what will be the value of sec θ?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

5 cos θ = 4 sin θ

**Formula used:**

cotθ = B/P

cotθ = cosθ/sinθ 

H² = B² + P²

**Calculation:**

5 cos θ = 4 sin θ

⇒ cosθ/sinθ = 4/5

⇒ cotθ = 4/5 = B/P

Now,

H2 = B2 + P²

⇒ H² = (4)² + (5)²

⇒ H² = 16 + 25 = 41

⇒ H = √41

secθ = H/B = √41/4

**∴ The required value is** **frac{sqrt{41}}{4}**

questions.question: AB is 12 cm long chord of a circle with centre O and radius 10 cm. The tangents at A and B intersect at P. What is the length of OP?
questions.solution:

AB = 12 cm

Radius = 10 cm

The tangents at A and B intersect at P.

**Concept used:**

**AAA similarity:** If all three angles in one triangle are the same as the corresponding angles in the other, then the triangles are similar.

Now,

OP ⊥ AB

So, OP bisects AB

AL = BL = 6 cm

Also,

OL = √(OA)² – (AL)²

⇒ OL = √(10)² – (6)²

⇒ OL = √100 – 36

⇒ OL = √64

⇒ OL = 8 cm

Now,

In ΔOAP and ΔOLA

∠OAP = ∠OLA

OA = OB = 10 cm (Radius)

OL = OL [Common]

So, ΔOAP ~ ΔOLA 

⇒ OP/OA = OA/OL [Corresponding sides are proportional]

⇒ OP/10 = 10/8

⇒ 8 OP = 100

⇒ OP = (100/8) cm

⇒ OP = 12.5 cm

**∴ The length of OP is 12.5 cm**

questions.question: Ramesh saves 26(2)/(3)\% of his monthly salary. When his expenses are increased by 20%, he is able to save Rs. 4,080 per month. His monthly salary is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Salary saves = 26(2)/(3)\% = 80/3

Expenses increases = 20%

Saving after increase in expenses = Rs. 4,080

**Calculation:**

Let the salary be Rs. 100

Saving = Rs. 80/3

Expenditure = Rs. (100 – 80/3)

⇒ Rs. (300 – 80)/3 = Rs. 220/3

New expenditure = Rs. (120% of 220/3)

⇒ Rs. (120/100 × 220/3)

⇒ Rs. (4 × 22)

⇒ Rs. 88

New saving = Rs. (100 – 88) = Rs. 12

Now,

⇒ 12% = 4,080

⇒ 12/100 = 4,080

⇒ (4,080 × 100)/12

⇒ Rs. (340 × 100)

⇒ Rs. 34,000

**∴ The required monthly salary is Rs. 34,000**

questions.question: If x + y = 27 and x² + y² = 425, then the value of (x - y)² will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x + y = 27

x2 + y2 = 425

**Formula used:**

(x + y)² = x² + y² + 2xy

(x – y)² = x² + y² – 2xy

**Calculation:**

(x + y)2 = x2 + y2 + 2xy

⇒ (27)² = 425 + 2xy

⇒ 729 = 425 + 2xy

⇒ 2xy = 729 – 425

⇒ 2xy = 304

Now,

(x – y)2 = x2 + y2 – 2xy

⇒ (x – y)² = 425 – 304

⇒ (x – y)² = 121

**∴ The required value of (x – y)² is 121**

questions.question: If (cosec² theta)/(cosec² theta - cot² theta)=(13)/(4),0circ , then the value of (52 cos² theta-9 tan² theta)/(18 sec² theta + 8 cot² theta) will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

(cosec² θ)/(cosec² θ - cot² θ)=(13)/(4),0circ

**Formula used:**

cosec²θ = 1/sin²θ 

cot²θ = cos²θ/sin²θ 

1 – cos²θ = sin²θ 

B² = H² – P²

**Calculation:**

(cosec² θ)/(cosec² θ - cot² θ)=(13)/(4),0circ

⇒ 1/sin2θ/1/sin2θ – cos2θ/sin2θ = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin²θ/(1 – cos²θ)/sin²θ = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin²θ/sin²θ/sin²θ = 13/4

⇒ 1/sin²θ = 13/4

⇒ sinθ = 2/√13 = P/H

Now,

B2 = H2 – P2

⇒ B² = (√13)² – (2)²

⇒ B² = (13 – 4) = 9

⇒ B = 3

Now,

cosθ = B/H = 3/√13

tanθ = P/B = 2/3

secθ = H/B = √13/3

cotθ = B/P = 3/2

Now,

The value of (52 cos² theta-9 tan² theta)/(18 sec² theta + 8 cot² theta)

⇒ 52 × (3/√13)² – 9 × (2/3)²/18 × (√13/3)² + 8 × (3/2)²

⇒ (52 × 9/13 – 9 × 4/9)/(18 × 13/9 + 8 × 9/4)

⇒ (36 – 4)/(26 + 18)

questions.question: If the number 645A2879B8 is divisible by both 8 and 9, then the smallest possible values of A and B will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The number 645A2879B8 is divisible by both 8 and 9

**Concept used:**

**Divisibility rule of 8 -** If the last three digits of a number are divisible by 8, then the number is completely divisible by 8

**Divisibility rule of 9 -** If the sum of digits of the number is divisible by 9, then the number itself is divisible by 9

**Calculation:**

According to the divisibility rule of 8, we have 9B8 should be divisible by 8

So, by option we saw that the smallest possible values of B is 2

So, B = 928, which is completely divisible by 8.

Now,

Updated number = 645A287928

According to divisibility rule of 9, sum of digits of the number should be divisible by 9.

Sum of digits = 6 + 4 + 5 + A + 2 + 8 + 7 + 9 + 2 + 8

⇒ Sum of digits = 51 + A

To make the number divisible, let us put the value of A

⇒ 51 + 3 = 54 (divisible by 9)

So, The smallest possible values of A and B will be A = 3 and B = 2.

**∴ The required value is A = 3, B = 2**

questions.question: The speed of a car is 40% more than that of a bus. A train covers 1020 km in 8(1)/(2) hours. How much distance will the car cover in 1(3)/(4) hours if the speed of the bus is half the speed of the train?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of car = 40% more than that of a bus

Time taken to cover 1020 km = 8(1)/(2)hours = 17/2 hours

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance/Time

**Calculation:**

Let the speed of bus be 100x

Then,

The speed of a car is 40% more than that of a bus = (140% of 100x)

⇒ (140/100 × 100x) = 140x

Speed of car = 140x

Now,

According to the question

The speed of the bus is half the speed of the train = (100x × 2) = 200x

The ratio of car, bus and train = (140x : 100x : 200x)

⇒ 7x : 5x : 10x

Now,

Speed = Distance/Time

⇒ (1020/17/2)

⇒ (1020 × 2)/17

⇒ 120 km/h

Speed of train = (120/10x) = 12x

Now, Speed of bus = 5x = 5 × 12 = 60 km/h

Speed of car = 7x = 7 × 12 = 84 km/h

Now,

The speed of car covers in 1(3)/(4) hours = (84 × 7/4) km

⇒ (21 × 7) km

⇒ 147 km

**∴ The required distance is 147 km**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

We know 40% = 2/5 and 

speed of a car is 40% more than that of a bus, so

Speed of bus is 5 unit and speed of car is 7 unit,

According to the question, speed of train is 1020/8.5 = 120 km/hr

So, speed of bus is 120/2 = 60 km/hr

So, 5 unit → 60 km/hr

Then, speed of car 7 unit → 60/5 × 7 = 84 km/hr

Now, the car covers in 1(3)/(4) hours is (84 × 7/4) = 147 km

questions.question: The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 5 years at the rate of 10% per annum is half the compound interest on Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at the rate of 10% per annum, interest compounded yearly. The sum placed on simple interest is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The simple interest on a certain sum of money for 5 years at the rate of 10% per annum is half the compound interest on Rs. 5,000 for 2 years at the rate of 10% per annum, interest compounded yearly

**Formula used:**

SI = (P × R × T)/100

CI = P(1 + R/100)T – P

Where, P = Principal, R = Rate, T = Time

**Calculation:**

CI = P(1 + R/100)T – P

⇒ 5000(1 + 10/100)² – 5000

⇒ 5000(110/100)² – 5000

⇒ (5000 × 11/10 × 11/10) – 5000

⇒ Rs. 6050 – 5000

⇒ Rs. 1050

Now,

SI is half the CI = Rs. (1050 × 1/2) = Rs. 525

Now,

SI = (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 525 = (P × 5 × 10)/100

⇒ 525 = 50P/100

⇒ P = Rs. (525 × 100)/50

⇒ P = Rs. 1050

**∴ The sum placed on simple interest is Rs. 1,050**

questions.question: AB is the diameter of a circle of radius 9 cm. PQ is a chord (not a diameter) that intersects AB at M perpendicularly. If AM : BM = 5 : 4, then the length of chord PQ will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

AB is the diameter of a circle of radius 9 cm

PQ is a chord (not a diameter) that intersects AB at M perpendicularly

AM : BM = 5 : 4

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8dc8becb1932a3db0526decb50176e05e69f6ed6075dd1c6e6530ee25a073b40.png] 

Let the ratio of AM and BM be 5x and 4x respectively

Then,

AB is the diameter of a circle of radius 9 cm = (9 × 2) = 18 cm

⇒ (5x + 4x) = 18

⇒ 9x = 18

⇒ x = 2

Now,

AM = 5x = (5 × 2) = 10 cm

BM = 4x = (4 × 2) = 8 cm

Now,

PM = MQ (AB is the diameter of the given circle and PQ is the perpendicular on AB)

As we know,

⇒ PM × MQ = AM × MB

⇒ PM × PM = 10 × 8

⇒ PM² = 80

⇒ PM = 4√5 cm

Now,

PQ = 2PM

⇒ PQ = (2 × 4√5) cm

⇒ PQ = 8√5 cm

**∴ The required value of PQ is 8√5 cm**
